title: Defaults for the Common Case
content:
What problem does this solve?
Many dispatch calls share a common status or log level. Default parameter values let callers omit the everyday argument while still overriding it when needed. Keyword arguments bind by name so you can skip or reorder optional inputs clearly.

Previously in your program
Lesson 16 required every argument at the call site. Now some parameters can declare a fallback in the def header.

Basic syntax
  def mark_route(destination, status="Review"):
      return f"{destination}: {status}"

  mark_route("Gloamfen")
  mark_route("Ash Ford", "Ready")
  mark_route(destination="Marsh Road", status="Denied")

What actually happens
Required parameters come before defaulted ones. Omitting an optional argument uses its declared default. Passing a value overrides that default. Keywords bind by name: mark_route(destination="Marsh Road", status="Denied") does not rely on position. Mutable defaults such as lists or dictionaries can be dangerous later; this lesson uses safe immutable defaults like strings and numbers. The None-sentinel pattern comes in a later lesson.

When this is useful
Add a default when one value is common but still worth making visible in the signature.
concepts: Required parameters come before defaulted parameters
Omitting an optional argument uses its declared default
Passing a value overrides the default

examples.title: Common status
examples.code:
def mark_route(destination, status="Review"):
    return f"{destination}: {status}"

print(mark_route("Gloamfen"))
print(mark_route("Ash Ford", "Ready"))
examples.explanation: The first call uses the default Review. The second overrides status.

examples.title: Keyword override
examples.code:
def log_entry(message, level="NOTICE", source="field"):
    return f"[{level}][{source}] {message}"

print(log_entry("gate checked"))
print(log_entry("tower signal", source="north tower"))
examples.explanation: Keywords let you override source while keeping the default level.

common_mistakes: Putting a defaulted parameter before a required one
Implementing a fallback only inside the body instead of in the signature
Forgetting that keywords bind by name, not by leftover position alone
Using a mutable list or dict as a default value

exercises.title: Use the declared default
hints: Only destination is passed at the call site.
status therefore uses its declared default.

exercises.title: Which signature is valid?
exercises.prompt: Which function signature is valid in Python?
exercises.success_message: Correct — required parameters come before defaulted parameters.
exercises.failure_message: Required parameters must come before parameters that declare defaults.
hints: Defaults fill in missing trailing arguments.
A required name cannot sit after a defaulted one.
Choose the signature with message first, then level="NOTICE".

exercises.title: One item by default
exercises.prompt: Fill in the second parameter so format_supply("rope") prints 1 x rope using a signature default (not a body fallback).
hints: The body already uses the name quantity.
Declare quantity in the header with a default of 1.
Write quantity=1 in the parameter list.

tests.message: Callers must still be able to override quantity.

exercises.title: Required before optional
exercises.prompt: This definition is invalid because a defaulted parameter appears before a required one. Fix the parameter order so destination is required and status defaults to "Review".
hints: destination should be first; status should keep its default.

tests.message: mark_dispatch("Gloamfen") should use the default status.
Positional override of status must work.
Keyword arguments must bind by name.

exercises.title: Dispatch log entry
exercises.prompt:
Write log_entry(message, level="NOTICE", source="field") that returns:
  [<level>][<source>] <message>

Support positional overrides and keyword overrides. Do not print.
exercises.success_message: Log line ready — common defaults stay convenient, and overrides stay clear.
hints: Keep the parameter names and defaults exactly as specified.
Build one f-string that inserts level, source, and message.

tests.message: Build the log line with an f-string inside log_entry.
A positional level override must replace NOTICE.
A keyword source override must keep the default level.
Keyword overrides must bind level and source by name.
